newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit extends gains as Mahathir resumes attack.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit extends gains as Mahathir resumes attack.

text.p: * The ringgit extended its gains of the last two days as some investors booked profit on their long dollar positions
* Sentiment affected by Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's unceasing tirade against speculators
The ringgit resumed its recovery on Wednesday as some recent investors booked profit in all regional currencies, dealers said.
"All dollar/regionals are coming back. Talk is some of the hedge funds are unwinding long dollar positions," said a dealer with a European bank in Singapore.
He said Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's relentless verbal attack against speculators, particularly U.S. financier George Soros, was having an effect on the market.
"The market feels that if he continues to talk this way there may be some action down the line. So people are wary," said an analyst with a research firm in Singapore.

Research firm I.D.E.A. said there was talk that the U.S. was asking hedge funds to unwind from long dollar/regionals positions to strengthen the position of its Secretary of State Madeleine Albright as she tours the region.
One analyst said technicals also pointed to a lower dollar/ringgit. He said ringgit was headed for 2.61 per dollar with a lot of stops expected to be triggered at 2.6050.
At 0300 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.6170/200 to a dollar.
